key_insight: Stacking ensembles delivered the most accurate task-specific predictions for UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness, while the multitask neural network provided strong shared-learning performance across all three targets.
engineering_relevance: For welding process optimization, the results show a practical trade-off between high-accuracy single-task prediction and efficient multi-output modeling for related mechanical properties.
method: Compared a multitask neural network (shared hidden layers, task-specific outputs) against stacking ensemble learning.
Used a common welding dataset to predict UTS, weld hardness, and HAZ hardness simultaneously or separately.
Evaluated both models with RMSE and R² to assess predictive accuracy and generalization.
evidence_signal: Stacking achieved lower errors and higher R² overall, including UTS RMSE 0.0263 (R² 0.9863), weld hardness RMSE 0.0467 (R² 0.9782), and HAZ hardness RMSE 0.1109 (R² 0.8453), outperforming MTNN on individual-task accuracy.
watch_item: The best model choice depends on the objective: stacking is stronger for precise task-by-task prediction, while MTNN may be preferable when data are limited and the outputs are strongly related.
paper_title: A Comparative Analysis of Multitask Neural Networks and Stacking Ensemble Learning for Predicting UTS, Weld Hardness, and HAZ Hardness in Welding Applications
